stories.title: U.N. Fact-Finding Mission Finds Evidence U.S. Committed War Crimes in Iran
stories.summary: A UN Fact-Finding Mission issued findings that the United States committed war crimes in Iran, including a strike on a school in the southern city of Minab. The findings come amid continued escalation in the Iran-U.S. conflict, with Iran striking multiple ships in the Strait of Hormuz in response. The incidents highlight mounting humanitarian concerns as regional tensions remain high and negotiations between the two countries have stalled since June.

stories.title: Congress Approves Sweeping New Sanctions on Russia and Iran
stories.summary: The U.S. House of Representatives passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by a vote of 262-159, following Senate passage with an 86-11 margin. The legislation targets Russian financial institutions, energy sector, and shadow fleet tankers, while authorizing the president to impose tariffs up to 100 percent on major purchasers of Russian oil and gas. Russia has signaled that signing the bill would make peace negotiations with Ukraine more difficult.

stories.title: Russia Continues Bombing Civilian Sites as Ukraine Retaliates with Drone Attacks on Oil Facilities
stories.summary: Russian military forces continued bombing civilian targets in Ukraine on September 18, while Ukrainian forces responded with drone attacks targeting Russian oil infrastructure and military facilities. The escalating campaign reflects the ongoing intensity of the conflict now in its eighth month, with both sides inflicting damage on civilian and strategic infrastructure. The pattern demonstrates the sustained military engagement despite periodic negotiation attempts.

stories.title: Polish PM Warns Russia Planning Hybrid Strikes on NATO-Supporting European Countries
stories.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that Russia is planning hybrid attacks—cyber operations, sabotage, and covert strikes—on European countries supporting Ukraine. Tusk stated Russia intends to disguise these attacks as accidents to weaken NATO members' political support for Kyiv. The warning reflects Europe's growing concern about escalating Russian operations beyond traditional military theaters as tensions continue over the Ukraine conflict.

stories.title: South Korea Refuses to Deploy Troops for Iran War
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung declared that South Korea will not deploy military troops or assets to support the United States in its ongoing conflict with Iran. The statement reflects Seoul's cautious stance on regional military involvement and maintains South Korea's independent foreign policy position. The declaration comes as the Trump administration seeks coalition support for operations in the Middle East.

stories.title: White House Withdraws Nomination of Lance Schroyer to Lead Immigration and Customs Enforcement
stories.summary: The White House withdrew its nomination of Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, to lead Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The announcement came amid ongoing scrutiny of the agency's operations and policies. The withdrawal follows public debate over ICE leadership and the Trump administration's aggressive immigration enforcement agenda.
